Important points in Previa management:

•Previa/ low lying @ place where blood available.
•Senior surgeon in presence of consultant
•Tocolysis for the purpose of completion of steroid
•Correction of anemia antenatal, women with atypical Ab – in liaison with hematologist and blood bank.
•Anterior placenta – more PPH.
•Anesthesia: Regional can be given.
•Local hematologist involvement.

Surgical Approach:

•Classical: before 28 weeks, traverse lie.
•Early cord clamping – if placenta is cut.
•PPH control:
⇨Pharmacological.
⇨Surgical measures.
⇨Intervention Radiology.
•Early recourse to hysterectomy.
→Balloon tamponade success 75 – 88%.

Combined balloon tamponade and B – lynch is more effective.

Diagnosis of PAS:

Undiagnosed 1/2 - 1/3rd cases.

1.USG:
-Highly accurate:
⇨Sensitivity = 90%.
⇨Specificity = 98%.
-Loss of clear zone.
-Abnormal Placental lacunae – moth eaten.
-Bladder wall interruption.
-Myometrial thickening < 1mm.
-Placental lacunae.
→Best specificity urinary bladder interface = 99%

TVS is superior:

It improves accuracy of TAS:

⇨Sensitivity – 87%.
⇨Specificity – 98%.

Indications of TVS

•TAS in-conclusive.
•Obesity.
•Fibroid.
•Posterior placenta.
2.Doppler ultrasound:
-UV – hyper vascularity.

-Sub placental hypervascularity.
-Bridging vessels.
-Placental lacunae.
→Best specificity is of abnormal vasculature:
⇨Sensitivity = 90%.
⇨Specificity = 87%.
→Power Doppler = intra placental hypervascularity
3.MRI:
•Diagnostic value is similar to USG that is performed by expert.
•Compliments ultrasound findings
•Assess deep tissue penetration in lateral and posterior placenta. It recognizes transverse cervical ligament penetration

Sensitivity = 75 – 100%

Specificity = 65 – 100%

Care bundle:

1.Consultant obstetrician.
2.Consultant anesthetist.
3.Blood and products.
4.Consent regarding
-C/section.
-Hysterectomy, blood tx, PPH.
-Urinary Tract injuries.
-Additional procedures.
⇨IOCS.
⇨Intervention Radiology.
⇨Visceral damage repair

 

Surgical Management:

1.Delivery of baby + P0 Hysterectomy.
2.Delivery of baby + myometrium resection (if limited invasion and area is assessable).
3.Delivery of baby and leave placental inside.
4.Leave placenta + II0 Hysterectomy 3-7 days later

Surgical precautions

⇨Ureteric stenting if placenta invading the bladder => recommended as risk of urinary track injuries = 14%
⇨Planned cystectomy can prevent extensive damage
⇨Intervention Radiology => in patients who refuse blood transfusion.
⇨Triple P procedure:
1.Pre – op placental localization.
2.Pelvic devascularization.
3.Placental non – separation.

•Internal iliac ligation => preserve uterus 90%
⇨Undiagnosed PAS during CS:

 

 

Close abdomen and refer:

-If diagnosed after delivery of baby, then leave placenta in situ and do hysterectomy.
